t: Earliest Second to Mark Indices I — Binary Search on Time + Greedy Check
o: Each second we either decrement some `nums[i]`, mark `changeIndices[s]` (only if it's already 0), or idle. An index can only be marked at seconds where it appears in `changeIndices`, and clearly we should use each index's **last** appearance within our budget `t` as its marking second — marking earlier only wastes flexibility. Feasibility for a fixed `t`: every index must appear in the first `t` seconds, and total work is `sum(nums) + n` seconds, but decrements for index `i` must all occur before its marking second. Greedy scan: accumulate 'free' seconds; when reaching a last-occurrence second, require enough free seconds to have covered `nums[i]` decrements. Examples confirm: for `[2,2,0]` the answer is 8; for `[0,1]` with `changeIndices=[2,2,2]`, index 1 never appears → -1. With `n, m ≤ 2000`, binary search over `t` with an O(n+m) check is fast.
k: Marking at the last occurrence of each index is optimal for feasibility.
Monotonicity: if time t suffices, any larger t does too — enabling binary search.

a.i: Feasibility is monotone in `t`, so binary search the earliest feasible second. The check greedily assigns all non-marking seconds to decrements, verifying each index's decrements finish before its forced marking second.
s: In check(t): record the last occurrence ≤ t of every index; fail if some index never appears.
Scan seconds 1..t: increment a free counter on ordinary seconds; on a last-occurrence second require free ≥ nums[i] and consume nums[i].
a.t: O((n + m) log m) — binary search over t, each check is linear

a.n: Approach 2: Linear scan of t with incremental check
a.i: Instead of binary search, increase `t` one at a time and maintain the last-occurrence structure incrementally. Worst case O(n·m) but avoids re-scanning; acceptable given constraints and simpler to reason about.
s: For t = 1..m, update last occurrences and re-run the greedy scan.
Return the first feasible t, or -1.
a.t: O(n·m) worst case — rescanning each candidate t

w: The crucial insight is forcing marks onto last occurrences — otherwise the exchange argument fails. Common bugs: forgetting that an index absent from `changeIndices` makes everything impossible, and integer overflow of `sum(nums)` (up to 2·10^12). Harder version (#3049) raises constraints so the check must become O(log) with smarter data structures.
